summary: France supports renewables mainly through contracts for difference set by reference tariffs, with feed-in tariffs kept for small plants. Repatriation of capital is unrestricted. The next multiannual energy programme was still pending in the sources reviewed.

access.reason: Large plants receive a premium on top of market sales under contracts for difference, which replaced the purchase obligation from 2015.

terms.reason: The premium is calculated against a reference tariff set by ministerial order for each technology.

ownership.reason: There is no restriction on repatriating capital when the investment is authorised and goes through an approved bank.

stability.reason: The next multiannual energy programme for 2024 to 2033 was still to be adopted when the sources were written.

direction.reason: No change to the support scheme was found in the sources reviewed.

access.reason: Small plants keep feed-in tariffs under the purchase obligation.

stability.reason: The energy programme update was pending.

direction.reason: No change was found in the sources reviewed.

events.title: Energy transition law moves support from feed-in tariffs to contracts for difference

sources.title: France Country Commercial Guide, trade financing

gaps: Grid connection times, buyer credit and corporate PPA practice were not covered. The CMS guide dates from March 2024, so later changes may be missing.
